goal: Repair native organic interface fragmentation at the user-observed 0.23 mm plane, preserving process parameters, brim and actual 0.17 mm contacts.

causes: Sparse organic interfaces selected a structural SupportBase fallback with return anchors instead of bounded rectilinear interface rows
Concentric fills used nominal-height spacing against actual-height wall keepouts
Rectilinear connections were generated before wall-clearance clipping, which split connections at concave corners
A compact generic interface projection had neither a same-plane connection nor any next-road/model demand

correction: Use native rectilinear organic interface rows with bounded support connections and no long parallel return anchors
Retain valid single-row regions through center-domain-aware epsilon insets without broadening the legacy narrow-rescue policy
Normalize concentric reference spacing and density together, preserving configured clear spacing
Plan interface fills directly within precomputed safe center domains; keep ordinary model-fill defaults unchanged
Preserve support/contact roles and actual-height flow; retain post-generation collision clipping
Use configured process width when testing compact narrow fallback paths
Remove only isolated compact generic interfaces with no same-plane road or later road starting at that Z
Protect true contacts, trunks, substantial platforms and any compact interface with actual downstream demand

regression_coverage: Independent heights and rotations with complete concentric rings and configured clear spacing
Concave rectilinear wall clearance without short fragments
Needed compact interfaces and true contacts retained; isolated orphan removed
Valid single-row organic interfaces remain straight without long parallel return anchors
Cooling, statistics and independent organic root handoff

scope_notes: This evidence concerns actual native geometry and Release instructions, not a physical printer measurement.
Configured 0.4 mm interface spaces and separate valid support regions are retained.
The full per-layer report records remaining short paths at other heights rather than treating every short path as an orphan.
